parameters.text:
=You are producing an actionable recon report for a security team, from an AUTHORIZED technical assessment of {{$json.target}}. No phishing, social engineering, or any technique targeting people (e.g. T1566, T1598, T1589, T1591) - this platform covers infrastructure/technical reconnaissance only.

HARD RULES:
- Never write "likely", "could indicate", "suggests", "may be", or similar hedge words about anything that is directly present in the raw data below. If a header is missing, say it is missing - don't soften it. If a status code was returned, state the exact code. If a string was found in a page, quote it exactly.
- Only hedge when data is genuinely absent or ambiguous (e.g. WHOIS returned nothing) - and even then, say exactly what's missing and what a follow-up check would need to resolve it, don't just say 'maybe'.
- Every entry in the Confirmed Findings section must cite the literal evidence (exact header name/value, exact status code, exact string, exact port/service) - not an inference.
- "No vulnerabilities were detected" is not a valid statement unless a vulnerability scanner actually ran (check attckCoverage/portScan/webScan for what was actually executed) - if nothing tested for vulnerabilities, say testing wasn't performed, not that none exist.

Given the raw JSON recon data below, produce a structured Markdown report with these sections:
1. MITRE ATT&CK Reconnaissance (TA0043) Coverage - table from the `attckCoverage` array, then 1-2 sentences on what TA0043 sub-techniques are deliberately out of scope (people/social) or unavailable (paid threat intel) and why.
2. Attack Surface Summary (2-3 sentences, facts only).
3. DNS, WHOIS & Subdomains.
4. Open Ports & Services (note if scan was skipped).
5. Confirmed Findings (Evidence-Backed) - the most important section. Go through `webScan.securityHeaders`, `webScan.cookies`, `webScan.contentDiscovery`, `webScan.fingerprint`, and `webScan.forms` and list every concrete finding as its own bullet, each citing the literal evidence:
   - Missing security headers (name each one from `securityHeaders.missing`, state what risk that specific header's absence enables - e.g. missing X-Frame-Options enables clickjacking, missing CSP weakens XSS mitigation).
   - Cookie issues (name each cookie missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite from `cookies`).
   - Content discovery hits: each entry in `contentDiscovery` has `status` and `distinctFromBaseline`. The scan first probed a deliberately-fake path to fingerprint what a non-existent page looks like (handles SPAs/servers that return 200 for every route - a raw 200 alone is NOT evidence). Only list a path as a real finding if `distinctFromBaseline` is true - state what that means (e.g. true 200 on `/.git/HEAD` distinct from baseline is a confirmed exposure; a 403 distinct from baseline means present but blocked). For any path where `distinctFromBaseline` is false, do not report it as a finding - note in one line that it matched the site's catch-all/soft-404 response and was excluded. If nothing in `contentDiscovery` is distinct from baseline, state plainly that content discovery found nothing real (the site returns identical content for arbitrary paths) rather than listing the raw 200s.
   - Fingerprint evidence (quote the exact strings from `fingerprint.evidenceStrings`, list versioned assets from `fingerprint.versionedAssets`).
   - Forms/parameter surface (for each entry in `webScan.forms`, state the exact action URL, method, and field names - this is the concrete input surface for injection/auth testing).
   If a category has nothing (e.g. no forms found, no missing headers), say so as a one-line negative finding, don't omit the category.
6. If I Were Attacking This - for EVERY confirmed finding in section 5, write one line in first person naming the exact tool and command/technique you would actually run against it, not an abstract MITRE label. Be specific and concrete, e.g.:
   - "No CSP or X-Frame-Options on {{$json.target}} - I'd host a clickjacking PoC page with an iframe pointing at the login form and see if it renders."
   - "`/.env` returned 200 - I'd `curl` it directly to pull whatever secrets are in it before doing anything else."
   - "`/.git/HEAD` returned 200 - I'd run `git-dumper http://target/.git ./dump` to pull the full source tree, then grep it for hardcoded credentials."
   - "Login form at /login posts `email`/`password` with no CSP - I'd run `sqlmap -u <action-url> --forms --batch --level=1 --risk=1` against it, and separately try `hydra -l admin -P <wordlist> <target> http-post-form '/login:email=^USER^&password=^PASS^:F=incorrect'` for a slow, rate-limit-aware credential attempt."
   - "Versioned asset `angular-1.2.3.js` found - I'd check that exact version against retire.js's known-vulnerable-library database / npm audit / a CVE search before assuming anything."
   - "Open port with an unclear/misidentified service - I'd run `nmap -sV -p<port> <target>` for a real version fingerprint, then `searchsploit <service> <version>` for known exploits."
   Only write an entry here for something that appears in section 5 AS A CONFIRMED finding (distinctFromBaseline true, or a header/cookie/form that genuinely exists) - never re-mention a path that section 5 excluded for matching the baseline. Don't invent findings, and never reuse an excluded path, to have something to attack. If there's genuinely nothing found, say plainly there's nothing actionable yet and what a broader scan would need to check.
7. ATT&CK-Aligned Next-Phase Plan - tie section 6's concrete actions back to the three ATT&CK tactics that follow reconnaissance. Every target named here must be one of section 6's actions, not a new or previously-excluded one:
   a. Resource Development (TA0042) - what infrastructure/tooling would need to be staged (e.g. a wordlist, a PoC page, a cloned repo) based on section 6.
   b. Initial Access (TA0001), non-human-targeting only - which of section 6's actions is the actual entry point attempt.
   c. Execution (TA0002) - what happens once that entry point succeeds, given the fingerprinted stack.
8. Caveats - state plainly what wasn't tested and what a broader scan or dedicated tool (ZAP, sqlmap against confirmed injectable params, credential brute-force) would add, referencing this platform's own capabilities where relevant.
Raw data:
{{ JSON.stringify($json) }}
